AMD.headline: Prediction: Here’s What Nvidia Stock Will Do After Its Projected $108 Billion Quarter Results Are Announced on Nov. 17
AMD.description: Nvidia is set to report Q3 earnings on Nov. 17 with projected $108 billion in revenue. Despite recent negative sentiment surrounding former CEO Jensen Huang's departure, analysts expect the company to beat expectations with 91% revenue growth. The stock is trading at an attractive 10x forward earnings multiple compared to the S&P 500's 18x, suggesting potential upside if the company meets expectations and addresses leadership concerns.

AMD.headline: Why Marvell Stock Is Down Today
AMD.description: Marvell stock fell 6.4% on November 16, 2026, as chip stocks broadly declined following Jensen Huang's departure as Nvidia CEO. Investors are rotating out of AI stocks ahead of Nvidia's earnings report. Additionally, Marvell's pending $115 billion all-stock acquisition of Lumentum is creating shareholder dilution concerns.

AMD.headline: Why AMD Stock Was Sliding Today
AMD.description: AMD stock fell 4.4% after the Commerce Department announced new chip export restrictions on Southeast Asia in response to Nvidia chips being illegally funneled to China. Since Singapore accounted for 12.4% of AMD's 2025 revenue, the company faces potential sales blocks or delays. The broader semiconductor sector also declined as the new restrictions threaten multiple chip manufacturers.

AMD.headline: ARM's 50% Licensing Revenue Surge Signals Strong AI-Driven Demand
AMD.description: ARM Holdings reported robust Q2 fiscal 2027 results with licensing revenues jumping 50% to $773M and total revenues rising 27% to $1.44B, driven by growing AI infrastructure demand and major licensing deals. Royalty revenues increased 8% to $670M, supported by wider adoption of Armv9 architecture. However, the company faces near-term volatility from licensing agreement timing and smartphone market pressures.

AMD.headline: MLCommons Releases MLPerf Training v6.1 Results, Spotlighting Recent Advances in AI Training
AMD.description: MLCommons released MLPerf Training v6.1 benchmark results featuring two new benchmarks: DLRMv4-HSTU for recommendation systems and Qwen3.5-397B for large-scale LLM post-training. The round achieved record participation with 153 systems from 24 organizations, including 37% cloud-based systems and the first submissions using NVIDIA Rubin-generation GPUs and Google TPUv7.

AMD.headline: Buy 3 AI-Led Giants on Robust Fundamentals and Short-Term Price Upside
AMD.description: Despite recent market volatility in the AI sector, three infrastructure companies—Snowflake, Dell Technologies, and Corning—are identified as strong investment opportunities with robust fundamentals and significant short-term price upside potential. All three companies benefit from strong AI data center demand, have raised guidance, and carry favorable Zacks Rank ratings of #1 or #2.

AMD.headline: If Staying in Nvidia Stock Scares You, You Might Want To Consider This ETF
AMD.description: Following recent controversies surrounding Nvidia's leadership, risk-averse investors concerned about holding individual chip stocks may consider the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) as an alternative. SOXX provides diversified exposure to 30 semiconductor companies with only 7.1% allocation to Nvidia, compared to 18% in competing VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH). The fund has delivered 32% average annual returns over 10 years with a low 0.33% expense ratio.

AMD.description: The Nasdaq Composite surged 2.3% last week, posting its strongest performance since early August, despite NVIDIA's continued decline following CEO Jensen Huang's departure. While wholesale inflation data came in softer than expected monthly, annual producer prices remain elevated. AMD.headline: AMD Earnings: What Wall Street Missed
AMD.description: AMD delivered record earnings with data center revenue nearly doubling and management forecasting over 80% growth in 2027, yet investors sent the stock sharply lower by 8.75%. The article explores the disconnect between strong business performance and negative market reaction, questioning whether AMD's $17 billion fourth-quarter target will prove the market wrong or expose risks behind its premium valuation.
